### Observed differences

- The three activities A14, A15 and A20 each ran in about 47 in 100 traces in the earlier window (94 of 200) but in essentially every trace in the later window (about 199 of 200). In both windows each occurs at most once per trace, and they appear together or not at all: earlier they were jointly absent from about 53 in 100 traces, in the later window from about 1 in 200. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL001, REL002, REL007]
- The order inside this group is unchanged: A14 runs before A20, and A20 before A15, in both windows — in roughly 47 of 100 traces earlier (when the group ran at all) and about 199 of 200 in the later window. [REL001, REL002, REL007, REL008, REL012]
- Routing out of A36 changed: earlier, its flow went to A14 in about 47 in 100 cases and directly to A21 in about 53 in 100; in the later window it goes to A14 in about 995 of 1,000 cases and to A21 in about 5 of 1,000. A36 and A21 themselves occur in every trace in both windows. [DIR001, REL003, REL004, REL013]
- The positional gap from A36 to A21 changed accordingly: earlier, A21 followed A36 immediately in about 53 in 100 traces and four positions later in about 47; in the later window it is four positions later in about 199 of 200 traces. [LAG001]
- Two further activities mainly track the group: A37 co-occurs with A14 in about 47 of 100 traces earlier versus about 199 of 200 in the later window, with a mixed order in both; A40 keeps an overall participation of roughly 60 in 100 but no longer appears in traces without A14 (about 33 in 100 traces earlier, essentially none later). [REL005, REL006, REL010, REL011, REL014, REL015]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the group A14 → A20 → A15, executed between A36 and A21, changed from optional to performed in nearly every case: earlier it ran in about 47 in 100 traces while A36 passed directly to A21 in the rest, whereas in the later window it runs in about 199 of 200 traces, A36 almost always leads into A14, and the direct A36 → A21 route survives in only about 1 in 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, LAG001, REL003]

The participation rise rests on large samples (94 versus 199 traces per activity) and is matched by the routing shift out of A36 and by the gap to A21 becoming uniformly four positions; all twenty qualifying items describe this one difference and its direct consequences, far more than the fewer than one item expected by chance across 76 tested units, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the same data. [OCC001, DIR001, LAG001, REL001, REL004]

Limitations: the evidence cannot show whether the direct A36 → A21 route was removed or only became rare, and it cannot rule out that the two windows cover different case mixes rather than a modified process; the roughly 1 in 200 later traces still without the group are too few to characterise. [REL003, LAG001]

Other differences: A37's order relative to A14 shifted somewhat (A14 first in about 30 of 100 traces earlier versus about 54 of 100 in the later window, with interleaving rising from about 17 to about 46 of 100), and A40 now occurs only in traces that also contain the group; both patterns largely follow from the group being present in nearly every later trace. [REL005, REL006, REL010, REL011, REL014, REL015]
